transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-09-02
Time: 10:00 PDT / 17:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Claire (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Marta (Nimbus Head of ML), Sam (Nimbus Platform), Evelyn (Nimbus PM)

00:00 - Claire: Hey everyone, thanks for jumping on. quick agenda — SDK integration status, results from Marta's test prompts, function calling quirks, and ops next steps. want to start with Diego for the SDK telemetry?
00:18 - Diego: Yeah, thanks Claire. Hi Marta, Sam, Evelyn. We ran your sample harness against the hosted instance and also against a small dedicated pool we spun up. I sent over a spreadsheet earlier but TL;DR: median token latency on hosted was ~85ms per token when streaming, dedicated dropped to ~48ms in the same sequence length distribution. There were a couple of outliers where the SDK retried and you can see a spike at 1.2s — that's due to transient cold-starts on the backend, not SDK-level retries.
00:45 - Marta: Okay that's helpful. Are the numbers from the latest SDK (v0.9.3) or the CLI shim we've been using? We're on 0.9.2 in our branch.
00:52 - Diego: Good call — results are a mix. The harness used v0.9.3 which includes improved streaming backpressure fixes; the CLI shim still using 0.9.2 will show more latency under heavy concurrency. I'll annotate the sheet which rows map to which client version.
01:10 - Sam: On the integration side we noticed occasional JSON malformation when using function-calling with our validators. Not huge but it trips our parser. Any known issues?
01:20 - Diego: We've seen that when the model returns 'loose' structured output — it's not a serialization bug in the SDK usually, more the model surface producing extra commas or trailing text. For function-calling mode we recommend adding a strict schema in the prompt and using the SDK's structuredOutput validation helper. There is also an option to request canonical JSON-only responses (we'll share the snippet).
01:41 - Evelyn: Can you walk through that snippet now? We tried the example in the docs but we might have misapplied the streaming variant.
01:48 - Diego: Sure. Quick pseudo code: use redwood.sdk.Chat.create with functionDefinitions, set callMode: 'function' and set responseFormat: 'json-strict', then on the client side pipe the partial chuncks into the structuredOutput.validate. The important bit is to close the stream only after validate returns success, otherwise you can get partial writes. (note: transcript may flip some variable names)
02:20 - Marta: Right, we had the stream close before validation finished — that explains the ragged JSON. We'll update the harness to wait for the final validate promise.
02:31 - Claire: There's also the question of retries; if a call fails during function invocation, do you want the SDK to re-run the same function or escalate to a human? What's Nimbus's preference?
02:41 - Marta: Prefer retries on idempotent ops, but for money-affecting steps we want a manual gate. Our use-case mostly annotates receipts and extracts structured fields — safe to retry.
02:52 - Diego: Perfect. We'll configure the SDK to do 2 automatic retries for errors that map to 429s or transient 5xx, and expose a hook for you to short-circuit in the client.
03:05 - Sam: On telemetry, we still don't see token-level cost broken down by route. The console shows an aggregate but our billing needs route-level split.
03:14 - Claire: We can expose per-route tagging — Diego, can you enable token tagging in the next build and share sample traces?
03:21 - Diego: Yep. I'll attach trace IDs in the CSV export. For privacy we will obfuscate PII but keep request/response sizes and latencies.
03:30 - Marta: About the function/tool calling — when we invoked external validators (your tool integration), sometimes the handler wasn't triggered and the SDK returned a normal text chunk. Is tool calling synchronous?
03:42 - Diego: Tool calling can be either sync or async. In your current harness it's synchronous — the model should produce a tool call event that the SDK maps to a handler. If the model instead outputs plain text, it's usually because the guidance in the prompt didn't strongly prefer tool usage. Two mitigations: 1) provide function usage examples in the few-shot context; 2) set toolPreference: 'force' in the SDK (we'll add note: this may change logits).
04:10 - Evelyn: Does forcing tool calls affect latency?
04:14 - Diego: Slightly. Forcing tool calls increases average response tokens and can add 10–30ms for the round-trip to the handler, depending on your handler's response time. If the handler is fast (sub-20ms) it's negligible.
04:35 - Marta: We also saw some divergence between Hosted and Dedicated where the structured output formatting was subtly different — like keys ordered differently which breaks our diff tests. Is that expected?
04:48 - Diego: There are a couple reasons: different kernel selections and quantization profiles can slightly affect token sampling for generative outputs. For structured JSON we recommend using deterministic sampling (temperature=0) and a post-processor that canonicalizes key ordering. We're also testing a 'json-canonicalizer' option in the runtime which can help — not GA yet but we'll put you on the alpha.
05:20 - Sam: Security question: for Dedicated can we have VPC peering and a managed key in our KMS? Also need audit log forwarding to our SIEM.
05:30 - Claire: Yes — Dedicated supports VPC peering and customer-managed KMS. Audit log forwarding is available via syslog/S3 connector. We'll share the architecture doc.
05:43 - Marta: Is there a compliance snapshot for the Dedicated control plane? We need SOC2 in the deck for procurement.
05:50 - Claire: I'll send the SOC2 summary and a short compliance FAQ. Note, the private/on-prem package has additional controls if you need air-gap later.
06:05 - Evelyn: Back to SDK specifics — we attempted to use streaming + function-calling concurrently and saw intermittent partial function payloads. Any known limitations?
06:18 - Diego: Streaming with function-calling is supported but historically we've had two edge-cases: 1) when a function payload exceeds the streaming chunk boundary and the client reassembles incorrectly; 2) when backpressure triggers a retry mid-stream. We pushed fixes in v0.9.3 — please move to that and enable the stream.reassembly helper. I'll add a code link in the follow-up.
06:51 - Marta: Great. For the structured output QA, can Redwood run a small job to validate our 200 sample prompts so we don't have to provision heavy infra? Could be just against Hosted but using our prompt set.
07:05 - Claire: We can run a verification pass on Hosted, but recommend running the canary on Dedicated to measure latency. Diego — feasibility?
07:12 - Diego: Yes — we can run a 200-prompt pass on Hosted first. That will give you coverage for format/regression. If you want latency SLOs validated we should do the Dedicated canary.
07:25 - Sam: On the Dedicated canary — what's the minimum config to get representative latency? We don't want to pay for a large pool.
07:33 - Diego: For your traffic profile (mostly short sequences, avg 60 tokens) a 1-GPU instance in a 2-node pool with 50 concurrent connections will be representative. We'll throttle to mimic burst patterns.
07:50 - Marta: Anything else on instrumentation? We noticed some interleaved logs in the SDK where trace IDs were missing.
07:58 - Diego: That was a known bug in 0.9.2 where async handlers didn't propagate the trace header to the child threads. Fixed in 0.9.3. If you still see missing trace IDs, send the logs and I'll trace the exact request IDs.
08:12 - Claire: Quick procurement note — Marta, you mentioned finance needs an SOW with a usage cap. We can draft a 30-day pilot SOW with a cap and optional roll-into Dedicated contract.
08:23 - Marta: That would help. Also please include a rollback/fallback clause if the canary causes production regressions.
08:30 - Claire: Will do.
08:35 - Evelyn: One last thing — structured outputs: our validator expects strict types (string vs int). The model sometimes returns integers as strings. Any tips?
08:44 - Diego: Two options: 1) enforce a strict schema and have the runtime coerce types when possible using the SDK's coercion rules; 2) run a post-validate transform that normalizes types. Coercion is in the SDK but we recommend explicit validation to avoid silent corruption.
09:06 - Marta: Ok. Let's recap next steps so our PMs and infra align.
09:11 - Claire: Recap: Diego will send telemetry + SDK sample for streaming+function calling (due 9/5). I'll send SOC2 snapshot and SOW draft (9/4). Marta will finalize sample prompts (9/6). We'll schedule the Dedicated canary for week of 9/8.
09:30 - Sam: noted. Thanks folks.
09:35 - Claire: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up in email with links.

Shared artifacts mentioned: https://redwood.company/s/secure/nimbus-poc-bench (spreadsheet, redacted), SOC2 snapshot (link to security doc), SDK v0.9.3 release notes link, canary run template (drive link).
